note: Rules behind the 'why this case?' hints. A rule applies when its trigger word comes right before the noun phrase (prepositions) or governs the object (verbs). Each rule needs native review before release.

hjá.en: hjá (at, with someone) always takes the dative.

úr.en: úr (out of) always takes the dative.

af.en: af (of, from) always takes the dative.

um.en: um (about, around) always takes the accusative.

í-staður.en: í (in) takes the dative for a location: where something is.
í-staður.nb: í (i) styrer dativ ved sted: hvor noe er.

í-hreyfing.en: í (into) takes the accusative for movement: where something goes.
í-hreyfing.nb: í (inn i) styrer akkusativ ved bevegelse: hvor noe går.

á-staður.en: á (on, at) takes the dative for a location.

á-hreyfing.en: á (onto, to) takes the accusative for movement.
á-hreyfing.nb: á (på, til) styrer akkusativ ved bevegelse.

eiga.en: eiga (to own, to have) takes its object in the accusative.
eiga.nb: eiga (å eie, å ha) tar objektet i akkusativ.
